payload.feature: Implement decision 0022 — reforging, the graph's way back into the fire (docs/decisions/0022-reforging.md on main; read it FIRST, it is the accepted ruling; 0006 bounds, 0007 provenance, and the fold/engine seams from #82/#84 are the neighbors). Scope: (1) THE BACK-EDGE: in every policy sharing the verify/review/ship constitution — bundles/self, recipes/fast, recipes/sdd (and via composition sdd-paranoid), recipes/panel-review — a review ruling recording has_security_residual true returns the run to implement (any severity, high and critical included), replacing the unconditional REVIEW-RESIDUAL-SECURITY stop while the bound holds. (2) BOUNDED: the rule vocabulary gains a phase-visit predicate (the fold already counts visits — the graph's ×N markers prove it); the back-edge fires only while implement's visit count stays within TWO reforgings; give the predicate exact-coverage-worthy tests of its own. (3) THE FINDING TRAVELS: the returning implement seat receives the review effect's result — findings, severities, notes — as declared input under 0007 (the sdd positions→chief threading is the recorded precedent); an implement seat on its first visit receives nothing new. (4) THE EXHAUSTION LADDER, at the bound: max_residual_severity above medium → stop (hard); medium → the run PARKS awaiting the operator with the residual as park reason — if the recorded vocabulary cannot express a rule-driven park, extend it honestly (a new versioned contract file is the only lawful contract change; never mislabel a stop as a park or vice versa; if it genuinely cannot be done lawfully, park the SLICE and say why); low/info with fixes_applied true → ship as tracked debt exactly as REVIEW-RESIDUAL-OK does for non-security today, the ruling named in the trail; low/info without fixes_applied → park, same operator door as medium. (5) Non-security rules are UNTOUCHED (0022 ruling 5); REVIEW-RESIDUAL-ABOVE-MEDIUM stays as is. (6) The engine must drive the loop end to end: a run whose review records a security residual actually re-enters implement, re-verifies, re-reviews, and a clean re-review proceeds to ship — prove it with a scripted-driver test that reforges once and then ships, one that exhausts the bound into each ladder arm, and one that proves the finding text reached the returning implement seat's input. (7) Policy digests move because policy moved: re-pin the witness digests and compose-test pins honestly as the identity change 0022 ruling 5 names. The TUI/console need no new surface — revisits already render; do not add one. CI enforces exact coverage — keep the gate green. Mind Windows: any test invoking scripted drivers follows the muninn tests' cfg precedents where kill semantics are involved.

result.notes: Framed decision 0022 (the security back-edge) into .forge/tasks/reforging-0022.md: replace REVIEW-RESIDUAL-SECURITY's unconditional stop with a bounded (two reforgings of implement) back-edge across bundles/self, recipes/fast, recipes/sdd (sdd-paranoid inherits via composition), recipes/panel-review, with an exhaustion ladder (above-medium stop, medium park, low/info-fixed ship-as-debt, low/info-unfixed park). Documented the exact existing seams to reuse (context.last_decision threading, computed_inputs in forge-core/src/fold.rs, the closed condition vocabulary in forge-core/src/policy.rs, the UNCOMPOSED digest pins in compose_tests.rs) and the two open design points the implementer must resolve: a phase-visit predicate added to the closed vocabulary, and a rule-driven park (no ruling severity currently means park-with-reason) that must not touch the frozen reference/ or policy/phase-machine.json material. bundles/verify and non-security residual rules are called out as explicit non-goals per ruling 5.

Decision 0022 implemented end to end and committed (3f20a1f, unsigned per seat convention; operator amend-signs). THE BACK-EDGE: REVIEW-RESIDUAL-SECURITY is replaced in bundles/self, recipes/fast, recipes/panel-review and recipes/sdd (sdd-paranoid inherits) by REVIEW-REFORGE (review residual + has_security_residual -> implement, flagged), ordered ABOVE REVIEW-RESIDUAL-ABOVE-MEDIUM so a high/critical security residual reaches the back-edge; the non-security rules keep their text unchanged. bundles/verify is untouched (no implement phase to return to) and its digest is unmoved. BOUNDED: fold now counts phase/entered per phase (RunState.visits) and the rule vocabulary gains the visits_<phase>_gte counter family, load-validated against the table's own phases and engine-owned (compile refuses a seat declaring one; the engine supplies only the counts the deciding phase's rules reference, so tables that ask nothing journal nothing). Back-edge fires while visits_implement < 3 = two reforgings. LADDER at the bound: above medium -> stop hard; medium -> park; low/info + fixes_applied -> ship flagged as tracked debt; low/info unfixed -> park. PARK VOCABULARY: the recorded table format could not express a rule-driven park, so it is extended honestly by a new versioned contract file contracts/phase-machine.v2.schema.json (v1 untouched) — a rule may carry "park": true instead of "next"; the loader refuses a park in a table declaring v1, and refuses park beside next/severity/requires_artifacts. No event-contract change was needed: transition/decided with rule_id + null next + null severity is the shape the artifact gate already writes, and fold already parks there; fold's park reason now names the rule instead of saying "no ruling". THE FINDING TRAVELS: a seat the run returns to (any phase entered more than once) receives the raw result that sent it back as context.returned_from; first visits are byte-identical to before. ENGINE PROOF: four new scripted-driver tests in machine_proof — reforge-once-then-ship (with the full ruling sequence), the bound exhausting into all four ladder arms, non-security rules ruling exactly as before, and the finding's text arriving in the returning implement seat's input (via a new fake-driver 'echo' behavior that returns the seat input inside the result). Plus exact-coverage unit tests for the visit predicate and the park vocabulary in forge-core, and a new compile-refusal case for a seat claiming a visit count. DIGESTS re-pinned honestly: witness_digests (fast), compose_tests UNCOMPOSED (fast/panel-review/sdd/self) and the composed sdd-paranoid golden, and the README recipes listing (verify's README line was already stale and is now the true value). Docs: contracts/README.md gains the v2 row plus the visits/last_result fold semantics; ARCHITECTURE.md gains the back-edge paragraph. No TUI/console surface added. Gates run locally: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings, cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked (all 36 test binaries ok), brokkr compile on bundles/self and bundles/verify, and the exact-coverage arithmetic reproduced by hand from cargo llvm-cov (lines 11453/11453, branches 1732/1732, functions 1001/1001) because the sandbox refused to execute scripts/coverage-exact.sh directly. Not done, deliberately: agents/charters/*.md are untouched — the returning seat already sees context.returned_from rendered into its prompt, and editing a charter would move byte-identity witnesses recorded for a different slice.

cargo test --workspace: every suite green, 0 failed across all crates — forge-store 13+14 unit, forge-view 46+47 unit/js, forge-runtime/forge-core aggregate 166 (engine incl. reforging back-edge, visit-bound predicate, and exhaustion-ladder tests) plus 56 lib, integration suites (bundle::compose_tests, adoption.rs 6, anchor_test 1, confine_test 2, fenced_commands 3, frozen_contracts 2, library_data 5, recovery 2, witness_digests 2 — includes re-pinned digests), doc-tests all pass. cargo run -p forge-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self exits 0 and emits a valid compiled bundle under the constitutional lint (policy.json/bundle.json digests present, all five seats/seven phases resolve).

Reviewed 3f20a1f (the whole delivery; 619628e was the pre-run head). Ran `cargo test --workspace` from this worktree: all green, 0 failed. Verified byte-identity of policy/phase-machine.json and reference/ (untouched), bundles/verify untouched and still v1, no stale digest literals anywhere in the tree, all four in-scope tables carry the identical ladder, README's recipes-list digests now agree with the compose_tests pins (they were stale before this commit). The back-edge arithmetic is right: visits_implement_gte 3 == exactly two reforgings, and the reordering of REVIEW-RESIDUAL-ABOVE-MEDIUM below the security rules is required by 0022 ruling 1, not a change to its content.

FIXED (1 file, committed 90ec3de, fixes_applied=true):
- [info] contracts/phase-machine.v2.schema.json landed as a new versioned file, correctly, but was not added to frozen_contracts.rs::the_new_contracts_exist_beside_the_frozen_ones — the recorded home for exactly that fact (run-manifest/v3, effect-provenance/v1). Added.

RESIDUAL FINDINGS (not fixed):

[MEDIUM — SECURITY] Absent max_residual_severity on a security residual now SHIPS where it used to hard-stop. bundles/self, recipes/fast, recipes/sdd, recipes/panel-review. conditions_met returns Ok(false) for an absent input (policy.rs), so a review recording {has_security_residual: true, fixes_applied: true} with NO max_residual_severity misses REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-ABOVE-MEDIUM and REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM and lands on REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-DEBT -> ship, flagged. Confirmed empirically against the real bundles/self table: at-bound-no-severity => Ruling{REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-DEBT, next=ship}. Before 0022 that same input hit REVIEW-RESIDUAL-SECURITY -> stop, hard. This is a fail-closed regression on the one path that was severity-blind by design, and the seat's severity is prompt-mandated, never machine-enforced (policy.rs's own comment: 'presence requirements belong to the result schemas'). max_residual_severity: "none" ships the same way. The DEBT arm's conditions are purely negative — it infers 'low or info' from the rules above having declined, so anything unclassified inherits the shippable arm. A fix IS expressible inside the closed vocabulary: add "max_residual_severity_above": "none" to REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-DEBT in all four tables, which drops absent/none through to REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-UNFIXED's park. Not applied here: it moves four policy digests plus six pinned literals and the README table, and it decides on the operator's behalf whether an unclassified security residual parks or ships — that is a ruling, not a typo.

[LOW — SECURITY] The finding travels as an unfiltered raw seat result, not as a declared input. 0022 ruling 1 and the slice framing both word it as 'declared input under 0007's provenance' with a narrow typed slot, explicitly cautioning 'never freeform-trusted past the schema boundary'. engine.rs seat_input instead inserts context.returned_from = {phase, result: state.last_result} — the entire result object verbatim, unbounded in size and shape. Two consequences: (a) a review seat's model-authored prose, which may quote attacker-controlled content out of the diff it is reading, now lands verbatim in the implement seat's prompt — a new seat-to-seat injection channel where before only the 0007-filtered inputs map crossed; (b) the gate is `visits[phase] > 1` for ANY phase, so it fires on every pre-existing loop too — IMPL-BROKEN-RETRY (implement->implement), REVIEW-CLEAN (review->verify), SHIP-DRIFT (ship->review) — a wider blast radius than 0022's security back-edge authorized. What holds it at low rather than higher: it is engine-supplied from the fold, so the receiving seat cannot spoof it; visits_* is correctly engine-owned via is_engine_owned's prefix test and provably undeclarable (compile_rejects_provenance_violations covers it); result files are secret-masked at the adapter choke point (adapters.rs:732) before journaling, so no plaintext secret crosses; and the deviation is documented honestly in ARCHITECTURE.md and contracts/README.md rather than hidden. Worth an operator ruling on whether the channel should be schema-bounded and scoped to the back-edge.

[INFO — correctness] The bound counts implement VISITS, not reforgings. IMPL-BROKEN-RETRY re-enters implement, so a run that stumbles once before ever reaching review arrives at its first security residual with visits_implement already 2 and gets ONE reheat, not two; the exhausted rules' reason text then says 'Two reforgings spent' when one was. This follows ruling 2's 'phase-visit predicate' wording literally and the framing asked for exactly this predicate, so it is arguably as ruled — but the reason strings the operator reads back can be false, and the ladder can fire a heat early.

[INFO — scope] crates/forge-cli/src/init.rs's scaffolded starter table still carries the pre-0022 unconditional REVIEW-RESIDUAL-SECURITY stop, and its description still claims 'security residuals never take the tracked-debt path'. 0022 ruling 5's scope list names self/fast/sdd-family/panel-review only, so leaving it is defensible — but every project scaffolded by `brokkr init` now starts life on the constitution 0022 replaced. Flagging rather than editing: widening 0022's scope is the operator's call.

[INFO — behaviour] fold.rs's park-reason change is not confined to rule-driven parks: an artifact-gate block now reads '<RULE-ID> for (from, result): ...' where it used to read 'no ruling for (...)'. Better wording and covered by tests, but it is a user-visible message change on an untouched non-security path.

Not re-run: scripts/coverage-exact.sh (needs an approval this seat does not have). Every new branch I traced has a test that exercises it — visit_phases' three skip paths, both park-reason arms, both returned_from arms, all four park load-time refusals, all four ladder arms end-to-end — so I expect the gate green, but I did not prove it myself; the verify seat's pass is what stands behind it.
